workload.description: 90% CDN-fronted image views, 1% uploads; derivative generation is the constraint

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: m6i.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); x86-64 (Intel Ice Lake). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.096/h x 730 = 7008c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.t4g.medium — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 8,000 req/s peak. Mix: 90% image views, 7% metadata/page loads, 2% manage (delete/edit/album), 1% uploads (~80 uploads/s peak, ~2.3M/day at average load)

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: CDN hit-rate 85% on image views, so 15% of views reach the origin tier; 70% of those origin hits are served from the metadata/signed-URL cache, leaving 4.5% of views to touch the object store

assumptions.subject: resize
assumptions.statement: One upload generates ~4 derivatives (thumb/small/medium/web). A 2-vCPU instance sustains ~20 uploads/s of derivative work end to end; this is the busiest component in the design

assumptions.subject: app
assumptions.statement: Image API ~1,500 rps/instance - mostly signed-URL minting and metadata reads, not byte pushing

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Cache instance count (2) is set for HA and working-set MEMORY, not for rps: at 1,800 rps it runs at ~2% of its request capacity. Do not read that as over-provisioning

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The SQL primary is modelled as ONE instance because there is one writer. A Multi-AZ standby is assumed in a real deployment but is NOT modelled as a second instance: it serves no traffic, and the engine would credit it with capacity it does not have. The engine will therefore flag the primary as a single point of failure - that flag is correct about failover, not about capacity.

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: 600 TB stored: ~9 months of accumulated uploads at ~2.3M/day x ~1 MB per image once originals and derivatives are counted

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: Delivery volume: ~80 KB average delivered object (thumbnails outnumber full-size views) x average view rate

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Monthly usage volumes (egress/storage/requests) are derived from AVERAGE load = peak / 3; capacity and instance counts are sized to PEAK. A single system_rps cannot carry both, so the peak:average ratio is stated here rather than hidden in a volume.

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Delivery egress is priced at the model's single flat internet-egress rate ($0.09/GB, the US first paid tier). At the petabyte-per-month volume this design implies, a real committed CDN contract is roughly 5-10x cheaper, so the egress line is an UPPER BOUND, not a quote. The volume (GB/month) is the engineering claim; the rate is not negotiated here.

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Per-request object-store charges (S3 GET/PUT) are NOT modelled. The model carries one request rate calibrated to an API gateway ($3.00/million); applying it to S3 requests would overstate them by ~7x. Add them with your own rate

_library.summary: CDN-fronted image upload and delivery service with asynchronous derivative generation.
